_meta.status: TEMPLATE v0 — every parameter value is a PLACEHOLDER. D-T06 measures the real limits; D-T03 populates both parameter sets; scripts/check_param_provenance.py enforces that every value traces to a measurement.
integrity_warnings: Parameter values must be DERIVED FROM MEASUREMENTS OF YOUR OWN RIG (data/calibration/rig-limits.json), never copied from a paper, a datasheet, or another project. A CI test (D-T06) checks the linkage and fails the build if a parameter has no provenance.

Every rule MUST have BOTH parameter_set_normal and parameter_set_degraded. Degraded values must be STRICTLY MORE CONSERVATIVE: lower limits, tighter bounds, shorter staleness windows, larger margins. A scripted diff asserts this (D-T19) — degraded mode is insight #3 made testable.

THE LAW: the envelope package must not import or reference any LLM client, HTTP client, socket, or network symbol. tests/test_envelope_purity.py walks the import graph and fails the build. Nothing in this file may introduce a network dependency.

Determinism: the same (SensorSnapshot, ActionProposal, envelope_version) MUST produce the same decision. No wall-clock time, no RNG, no dict iteration order, no floating-point accumulation order that varies. tests/test_envelope_determinism.py replays 500 snapshots twice in separate processes and compares hashes.
A rule whose required sensors are missing or stale FAILS SAFE (vetoes). Never skip a safety rule silently.

Test the NEGATIVE case as hard as the positive: a rule that fires on clean input is a false positive and will make the demo look broken. D-T24 measures the false-positive rate over 10 minutes of empty workspace and 10 minutes of normal operation.

This is a research prototype. It is NOT a certified safety system and does NOT constitute compliance with ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066, the Machinery Directive, or any other standard. That statement must appear in SAFETY-CASE.md, LIMITATIONS.md, the README first screen, and the video.
_meta.evaluation_order_rule: Evaluate in ascending priority. FIRST veto wins. Severity 'clamp' modifies the action and evaluation continues; severity 'hard_stop' or 'reject' terminates evaluation and the shipped action becomes a no-op.
_meta.envelope_version: TODO — set to sha256 of (this file + the envelope source tree) at build time, and embed it in every EnvelopeDecision so a decision can be tied to the exact rule set that produced it

modes.normal: Cloud reachable, sensors fresh, full parameter set.
modes.degraded: Cloud unreachable beyond V8's window, OR any sensor degraded. Same rules, stricter parameters, local model only, no multi-step plans. Degraded is a MODE, not an error — the rig keeps operating safely.
modes.simulation: Simulated sensors and actuator. The dashboard must show a SIMULATION badge permanently. Never let a viewer confuse this with hardware.

rules.description: An e-stop is asserted, or the interlock relay is open. Nothing else is evaluated.
rules.action_on_veto: Open the interlock relay (idempotent); command a no-op; latch until an explicit operator reset.
rules.rationale: The e-stop must be the first thing evaluated and must never be outranked. Latching matters: a momentary e-stop that auto-clears when the button is released is not an e-stop. This is the one rule whose behaviour is not a matter of tuning.
rules.false_positive_risk: Low. A wiring fault or a bouncing switch can assert it spuriously — debounce in hardware and in the driver, and record the debounce window as a measured value.
rules.tuning_note: The 20 ms staleness window is deliberately tight: an e-stop whose sensor state is 200 ms old is not trustworthy.

rules.description: An object or person is inside the marked keep-out volume.
rules.action_on_veto: Hard stop; open the interlock relay if severity demands; log the evidence (method, blob bbox, confidence) so the veto can be explained afterwards.
rules.rationale: The primary hazard for a bounded-workspace cell. Note that consecutive_frames_required stays at 1 in BOTH modes: requiring two frames of confirmation would delay a stop, and a delayed stop is worse than an occasional false positive. The degraded set instead LOWERS min_blob_area_px so that smaller intrusions trigger it — stricter detection, never slower reaction. Recording the evidence method is what makes the veto auditable rather than mysterious.
rules.false_positive_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH and lighting-dependent. Frame differencing fires on shadows, reflections, a hand reaching past the volume, and a passing cloud. Mitigate with diffuse lighting, a fixed camera, a background refresh policy, and the D-T24 study. Report the measured rate honestly.
rules.tuning_note: min_blob_area_px is the main knob. Set it from a measured object at the measured working distance; do not guess. A second independent witness (a microswitch or a tiny classifier) reduces both false positives and the risk of a single-detector blind spot.

rules.description: The commanded velocity exceeds the limit for the current mode.
rules.action_on_veto: CLAMP the commanded velocity to the limit and continue; record clamp_applied with before and after so a partial refusal is visible in the UI.
rules.rationale: Velocity is the single most effective lever on consequence severity: stop distance scales with it, and so does impact energy. Clamping rather than stopping keeps the cell productive while reducing risk — but a clamp MUST be visually distinct from an allow in the UI (D-T08), because a partial refusal that reads as success is a design failure. The degraded multiplier of 0.4 is a placeholder; derive yours from the measured veto-to-stop distance so that the degraded stop distance fits inside the keep-out margin.
rules.false_positive_risk: Low, but a noisy encoder can produce spurious high readings. Filter, and record the filter's latency as a measured value — filtering that adds latency to a stop is a safety cost.
rules.tuning_note: Derive the degraded value from the measured veto-to-stop distance at the normal limit, then choose a degraded limit whose stop distance is comfortably inside the keep-out volume. That derivation is the whole point of D-T06.

rules.description: Measured or estimated contact force exceeds the limit.
rules.action_on_veto: Hard stop; retract if a safe retract vector exists; open the interlock relay.
rules.rationale: Most Tier-2/3 rigs have no force sensor. Estimating force from motor current is a legitimate, explainable approximation — but you MUST label it as an estimate (force_estimate, not force_measured) everywhere it appears, and LIMITATIONS.md must say what it cannot detect. A slow contact against a soft object may not raise current at all. Claiming force sensing you do not have is exactly the kind of overclaim this project exists to avoid.
rules.false_positive_risk: MEDIUM if estimated from current: acceleration transients look like contact. Gate the check on a near-constant-velocity phase, or use a threshold above the measured acceleration transient, and record that transient as a measurement.
rules.tuning_note: Measure the stall current and the acceleration transient separately. The limit must sit above the transient and below stall. If those two are close, the check is not usable — say so and drop V4 to advisory rather than pretending.

rules.description: The commanded pose lies outside the allowed workspace envelope.
rules.action_on_veto: CLAMP the target to the nearest point inside the allowed volume; if the clamped motion would still exceed a margin, hard stop instead.
rules.rationale: The limit switches give a hard physical bound; the software envelope should stop well inside it so the switches are a last resort that never fires in normal operation. **If your limit switches fire during a session, that is a finding worth reporting** — it means the software envelope was too permissive. Shrinking the allowed volume in degraded mode is the clearest possible example of 'same rules, stricter numbers'.
rules.false_positive_risk: Low. Encoder drift can make the estimated position wrong — re-home periodically and record the drift you measure over a session (D-T06's repeatability measurement).
rules.tuning_note: Set boundary_margin_mm from the measured veto-to-stop distance plus the measured repeatability error. That sum is the distance you need to guarantee a stop inside the physical bound.

rules.description: The swept volume of the commanded motion intersects a detected object.
rules.action_on_veto: Hard stop before executing; log the predicted intersection so the veto can be explained and replayed.
rules.rationale: V2 stops when something IS in the keep-out volume; V6 stops when the motion would REACH something. For a single-axis pusher the swept volume is trivial to compute, which is why the in-house simulator (D-T04) is adequate. Doubling the lookahead in degraded mode is another clean instance of 'same rules, stricter numbers' — with less certain perception, look further ahead.
rules.false_positive_risk: MEDIUM: an inflated swept volume in a tight workspace can make legitimate motions impossible. Measure the inflation from the repeatability error plus the detection uncertainty, not from a guess, and report what fraction of intended motions it blocks.
rules.tuning_note: This rule and V2 will often fire together. Priority order means V2 wins — verify that with the D-T10 priority test, and note in the ledger's rule_trace that V6 was also evaluated. Showing the full evaluation trace is a novel and genuinely informative UI element (D-T28).

rules.description: Any required sensor has not produced fresh data within its window.
rules.action_on_veto: Fail safe: hard stop, enter degraded mode, and require a fresh sensor sweep before resuming.
rules.rationale: A safety system that acts on stale sensor data is not safe. Note the inversion: for V7, degraded mode makes the window SHORTER, not longer — a stricter tolerance for staleness when confidence is already reduced. The parameter must be derived from the MEASURED p99 sensor interval (D-T15), with margin. A window shorter than the normal frame interval causes constant false vetoes and makes the rig unusable.
rules.false_positive_risk: HIGH if the window is set below the real p99 frame interval. This is the most commonly mis-tuned rule in a hobby rig. Measure first, then set.
rules.tuning_note: Publish the measured sensor staleness distribution alongside the chosen window. That pairing is what turns a magic number into an engineering decision a judge can verify.

rules.description: The cloud planner or perception service has been unreachable beyond the window.
rules.action_on_veto: ENTER DEGRADED MODE: switch to parameter_set_degraded for all rules, refuse multi-step plans, use the local model only, and keep operating. **Never fail open.** Buffer decisions locally and back-fill on reconnect (D-T13).
rules.rationale: THIS IS INSIGHT #3 MADE TESTABLE, and it is the most important rule in the file for the submission's argument. A safety layer whose behaviour depends on network reachability has a network-dependent failure mode. The correct response to losing the cloud is not to stop (that is a denial-of-service on your own cell) and certainly not to continue with the permissive parameters (that is failing open) — it is to continue under STRICTER parameters with reduced capability. That is a real design position, it is defensible, and it is filmable by pulling a cable.
rules.false_positive_risk: Low, but a brief network blip should not flip modes. The window_ms debounce handles that; measure your real round-trip variance and set the window above it.
rules.tuning_note: A scripted diff (D-T19) asserts that EVERY degraded parameter is more conservative than its normal counterpart. If you add a rule later, that test forces you to define its degraded behaviour — which is exactly the discipline you want.

rules.description: The ActionProposal fails schema validation, has missing preconditions, is expired, or requests a limit above the envelope ceiling.
rules.condition: schema_invalid OR preconditions_unmet OR ttl_expired OR requested_limit > envelope_ceiling
rules.action_on_veto: Reject the proposal; do not execute; log it. Ask the planner for a new proposal (in normal mode) or fall back to a hardcoded safe sequence (in degraded mode).
rules.rationale: A cloud model's output is untrusted input to a machine that moves. Schema validation, precondition checks and expiry are the minimum hygiene. **The ttl is the interesting part**: a proposal issued five seconds ago describes a world that no longer exists, and executing it is how a stale plan causes an accident. A shorter ttl in degraded mode reflects less confidence in the world model. The 'requested limit above ceiling' check enforces the asymmetry that a planner may ask for LESS than the envelope allows but never MORE.
rules.false_positive_risk: Low. But an over-tight ttl causes rejections under normal cloud latency — measure your real planner round-trip (D-T22) and set the ttl above p99 with margin.
rules.tuning_note: Log every V9 rejection with the specific failure reason. A planner that produces many malformed proposals is a prompt-engineering finding worth reporting, and the rejection rate is a real metric for the quality of the structured-output integration.

rules.description: A person (hand, arm, face, body) is detected in or near the cell — a wider region than the keep-out volume.
rules.action_on_veto: Hard stop; open the interlock relay; latch until the region is clear for a hold time.
rules.rationale: Distinct from V2 because the region is wider and the response latches: an object in the keep-out volume stops the motion, a person near the cell stops the motion AND keeps it stopped until they have been gone for a hold time. Priority 10 looks odd for a human-safety rule — it is placed last because V1–V9 are all also human-safety rules and the priority order reflects *specificity of the hazard*, not importance. **Explain that in the video if a judge asks; it is a subtle point that shows the ordering was thought about rather than arbitrary.** Widening the region and lengthening the hold in degraded mode reflects reduced perception confidence.
rules.false_positive_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH. Distinguishing a hand from an intruder object with frame differencing alone is hard; a tiny on-device classifier helps (E1 has a real job here). Report honestly which method you used and what it confuses.
rules.tuning_note: If you film a hand entering the region, the velocity limit must already be set well below anything that could injure, and you should say so on camera. Filming an unsafe demonstration of a safety system is the worst own-goal available in this track.

global_invariants: A VETO's shipped_action is ALWAYS a no-op. Never the clamped action. Asserted in the schema.
A hard_stop VETO opens the hardware interlock relay. The relay is in the actuator's POWER PATH, not a software flag.
The envelope NEVER fails open. Any uncertainty — missing sensor, stale sensor, malformed plan, lost network — resolves toward stopping or degrading.
A cloud model's output can only make the envelope MORE conservative, never less. Cosmos Reason may add evidence; it may not clear a veto. Asserted by a test (D-T14).
The planner is NOT told the envelope's parameters. A planner that knows the limits will plan to them, which defeats the demonstration. Recorded in DECISIONS.md.
Every decision records envelope_version, so a decision can be tied to the exact rule set that produced it. This is what makes the ledger auditable across a changing codebase.
Every decision records the FULL rule evaluation trace, not just the rule that fired. Showing which rules were considered and in what order is a genuinely novel artifact.
Degraded mode reuses the SAME rules with STRICTER numbers. It is not a separate code path — a separate path would be a separate thing to verify.
non_goals: This is not a certified safety system and does not constitute compliance with ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066, the Machinery Regulation, or any other standard.
It does not protect against mechanical failure of the rig itself (a broken rail, a detached pusher, a failing PSU).
It does not protect against a hazard outside the monitored region.
It does not model dynamics accurately: the simulator is a simplified swept-volume model, so a replay proves that the envelope CHANGED THE OUTCOME, not the exact real-world consequence.
It does not handle multi-actuator coordination, human-robot collaboration with force-and-power limiting, or any mobile base.
It does not detect a transparent or very dark intruder reliably with frame differencing. Report this blind spot in LIMITATIONS.md.
It does not survive a failure of the relay itself unless you tested that case. If you did not test it, say so.

acceptance_checks.taxonomy_validation: python scripts/validate_taxonomy.py --strict  → 10 rules, total unambiguous priority order, both parameter sets present on every rule, every rationale ≥2 sentences, every rule has a named fixture and a false-positive note
acceptance_checks.parameter_provenance: python scripts/check_param_provenance.py → every numeric parameter traces to a measurement in data/calibration/rig-limits.json
acceptance_checks.degraded_strictness: python scripts/diff_parameter_sets.py → every degraded value is strictly more conservative than its normal counterpart; fails the build otherwise
acceptance_checks.purity: make verify-envelope → import-graph walk finds zero network/LLM symbols in edge/envelope/
acceptance_checks.determinism: 500 snapshots replayed twice in separate processes → byte-identical determinism_hash
acceptance_checks.priority: every simultaneous-fire rule pair resolves to the lower-numbered rule
acceptance_checks.per_rule: 10/10 rules pass their positive fixture AND do not fire on a clean-input negative fixture
